Abstract:

The design and synthesis of Schiff base ligands containing O- and N-donor atoms represent important strategies for advancing the coordination chemistry of transition and main-group metals. In particular, symmetrical and unsymmetrical N2O2 and ONO-donor ligands offer versatile coordination environments for tuning the structural, electronic, and biological properties of metal complexes. Incorporating diaminomaleonitrile (DAMN) into these frameworks enables further modulation of electronic properties through electron-withdrawing cyano groups and extended &amppi-conjugation. While transition metals such as vanadium, cobalt, nickel, and zinc have been widely investigated for their oxidation state versatility, photophysical features, and biological activities, main-group metal complexes particularly, those of tin and aluminium incorporating unsymmetrical Schiff bases remain relatively under explored. Motivated by these considerations, this study reports the design, synthesis, and characterization of novel symmetrical and unsymmetrical N2O2 and ONO-donor ligands along with their transition ((V, Co, Ni, Zn)) and main-group-metal (Al, Sn) complexes. The synthesized compounds were comprehensively characterized using spectroscopy, HR-ESI-MS spectrometry, and single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis. Furthermore, the biological potential of these complexes was evaluated through DNA/protein binding affinities, cytotoxicity evaluation, and cellular imaging studies.&nbsp
